answer: A daily routine that has genuinely benefited me is waking up early and having a calm, [[unhurried]] start to my day. I get up around six, well before I need to, which gives me time for myself before the world wakes up. Our neighbourhood is very quiet at that hour, apart from the birds and the odd rickshaw bell, and I really value that peace. I use this quiet period to plan my day, read a little and enjoy a proper breakfast rather than rushing. My mother is usually up too, so we often share the first cup of tea together before the rest of the family is awake. What makes it so valuable is that it sets a productive, positive tone for everything that follows. I keep it up by going to bed at a reasonable hour, since [[discipline]] at night makes the mornings easier. I also leave my phone in another room, so I am not tempted to stay up late scrolling. Honestly, starting the day calmly rather than in a panic has had a [[remarkable]] effect on my mood and focus. It gives me a sense of control that lasts throughout the day, and I rarely feel that I am chasing my own schedule. When I have skipped it, perhaps after a late wedding or a long journey, I can really feel the difference. I think how you begin your morning genuinely shapes the rest of it. This routine has become one of the most [[beneficial]] habits I have ever developed, and I would recommend it to anyone who feels [[perpetually]] rushed.

followUps.q: Is it hard to keep this routine at the weekend?
followUps.answer: A little. On Fridays I sometimes allow myself an extra hour in bed, but I try not to change my sleep pattern too much, because Saturday mornings then feel much harder.

followUps.q: Were you an early riser as a child?
followUps.answer: Not at all. My mother practically had to drag me out of bed for school. It is funny how things change; now I am often the first one awake in our flat.

note: Added quiet neighbourhood, tea with mother and the phone rule for keeping it up; moved mark from plain-ish 'productive' to [[unhurried]], added [[perpetually]].
